title: Klarna rehires human support staff after AI-first service lowered quality
summary: Klarna CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski told Bloomberg that the company's AI customer-service chatbot was cheaper than human staff but produced lower-quality output, and that Klarna is recruiting customer service agents again after a hiring pause of more than twelve months during which headcount fell 22% to about 3,500. He said there will always be a human available for customers who want one, a partial reversal of Klarna's February 2024 claim that the bot did the work of 700 customer service agents and handled 75% of customer chats, covering refunds, returns and payments in more than 35 languages.
verification_note: URL fetched on 2026-10-17; page dated May 09, 2025, published by Entrepreneur (Sherin Shibu), citing a Bloomberg interview with the CEO. The 22% headcount fall to 3,500, the 700-agent and 75%-of-chats claims, the refunds/returns/payments scope and the 'there will always be a human' quote are confirmed from the article body. The page names no AI vendor or model and calls the system a chatbot; included because it is a production customer-service deployment with transactional scope whose stated remedy is a human fallback.
